finding.copy_from: Append one filled examples.finding object to this array. Do not submit this wrapper or notes.

member_ids: a member id from the map
finding.consequence: What goes wrong for an agent because of it

finding.notes: Evidence entries illustrate locator choices, not mandatory sample files: replace the example array with the actual located references needed for this finding. Fill every judgement and use mapped member IDs. Submitting findings starts a separate correction stage; it does not complete the audit.

member_delivery.copy_from: Merge only examples.observed or examples.not_observed into that existing entry, then fill its fields. Do not submit this wrapper or notes.

observed.observation: What you saw the member do, where you saw it, and what you did not see

member_delivery.notes: Reading source alone is not observed delivery. With not_observed, omit observation and observed_at; remove any substantive sighting fields from a previous choice. For a sighting now, leave observed_at null or omit it. For an earlier sighting, replace null with its UTC time in audited_at's form. When the sighting is a dated record you read during this audit, such as a note or log of the mechanism acting, give the record's date, not the time you read it

recent_decision.copy_from: Replace the whole object with only examples.assessed or examples.unavailable, then fill its fields. Do not merge alternatives or submit this wrapper.

assessed.assessment: How the decision held up against the members' own words; when only a commit message records it, name the commit by its sha and subject here

evidence.path: a project file that records the decision; when only a commit message records it, the file that commit changed to carry it out
evidence.heading: optional exact heading

unavailable.unavailable_reason: Why no recent decision under this principle can be checked

reassessment: Give a reassessment only for a fixed finding; omit it for deferred, accepted or disagreed.

check_result.copy_to: response_template.member_assessments entry matching member_id, inside check_result
check_result.copy_from: Merge only examples.ran or examples.not_run into that existing object, then fill command and outcome. Leave unused fields exactly as that member's template printed them. For a new or changed run, write its review_basis; for an unchanged run, keep its own review_basis placeholder to retain the earlier line, or write a new basis. Do not submit this wrapper or limits.

ran.command: the member's check, exactly as context.members lists it

not_run.command: the member's check, exactly as context.members lists it
not_run.not_run_reason: Instead of exit_status, when you could not run it here: why, such as a missing tool or a sandbox

check_result.limits: Give a checked member's check_result in its own entry in member_assessments, where the template starts it, and none for a member without a check. A member that names a check asks for it to run at each full audit, however long it takes; if it is too slow to run at every audit, say so as a finding rather than skip it. Do not count on a permission prompt to show the command to anyone first. unchanged means an earlier audit ran this same command, not that it is safe: the audit record is committed too, and can be changed beside the check. Run the command in the project before you report its exit status: nothing runs it automatically, and nothing confirms that a reported run happened, that it ran on the files as they are now, or that the status is the one it returned. A failing check is a fact for your assessment; whether the member delivers stays your judgement.
